people.disambiguator: William A. Walsh's father, of Ardmore
people.summary: Born in 1837 at Ardmore, Ireland, he settled in Yonkers about 1853, worked as a carpenter and builder, and died there on 9 July 1916. Father of William Aloysius Walsh.
people.story:
Michael Walsh was born in 1837 at Ardmore, Ireland, came to the United States as a boy, and settled in Yonkers about 1853.[^findagrave-michael-walsh-1916] He worked as a carpenter and builder (Bowler and Walsh), served as a Water Commissioner, and was a leader in the St Vincent de Paul Society. He died on 9 July 1916 at 117 Palisade Avenue, Yonkers.

His 1916 Yonkers Statesman obituary, transcribed on Find a Grave, names his wife as Ellen E. Kelly and his sons as John J., Thomas A., and William A., a lawyer. The identification of that son with Mayor William Aloysius Walsh, father of Paul H. Walsh, is supported by William's own memorial, which names Michael as his father.[^findagrave-william-a-walsh] Other children named in the notice are not added to this tree in this pass.

birth.note: The obituary names Ardmore, Ireland, and does not give the county. The map uses the village of Ardmore in County Waterford, the usual place of that name.

people.disambiguator: Paul's father, Mayor of Yonkers 1926 to 1927
people.summary: Born 18 August 1871 in Yonkers, son of Michael Walsh. A lawyer, he was Mayor of Yonkers from 1926 to 1927. Husband of Clara F. Hingston and father of Paul H. Walsh. He died in Yonkers on 18 March 1967 and is buried at Saint Joseph's Cemetery.
people.story: William Aloysius Walsh was born on 18 August 1871 in Yonkers, the son of Michael Walsh of Ardmore, Ireland.[^findagrave-william-a-walsh][^findagrave-michael-walsh-1916] His mother was probably Ellen E. Kelly, named as Michael's wife in the 1916 obituary. He was a lawyer, and he served as Mayor of Yonkers from 1926 to 1927. The 1951 wedding notices of his son Paul call him former Mayor William A. Walsh of Yonkers, and his gravestone at Saint Joseph's Cemetery is inscribed Mayor 1926 1927.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1951-05-18][^findagrave-william-a-walsh] He married Clara F. Hingston in 1913, according to her memorial, and they were the parents of Paul Hingston Walsh. Social Security extracts also name the couple as the parents of William A. Walsh Jr., born in Yonkers in 1914, and Clayre Walsh O'Hara, born in 1917; those siblings are not yet added to this tree.[^ssa-numident-walsh] He died in Yonkers on 18 March 1967. The New York Times obituary of 19 March 1967 has not yet been read.

people.summary: Born in Italy, he raised a large family with Vincenza Guida at 44 Brambach Avenue, Eastchester, and died at Grasslands Hospital, Mount Pleasant, on 24 April 1944.
people.story:
Vincenzo Vigliotti, usually called Vincent in American records, was born in Italy and lived with his wife Vincenza, also called Winnie, at 44 Brambach Avenue in Eastchester, New York.[^ancestry-census-1930-vigliotti][^ancestry-census-1940-vigliotti] The 1930 and 1940 censuses record nine children in the household, including Alphonse.

His exact birth date and town are not yet settled. Census ages point to about 1886. His 1944 death notice says he was born in Italy fifty-three years earlier, which points to about 1891. A member tree gives 4 July 1885 at Santa Maria a Vico, in the province of Caserta, and names his parents as Andrea Vigliotti and Mariantonia Ruotolo. Those Italian details remain unverified until the civil register is read.[^ancestry-tree-kindred-spirits]

A New York passenger list index shows a Vincenzo Vigliotti, aged 17, arriving on the ship Roma on 1 April 1903. The manifest page has not yet been found on the roll, so the match is probable.[^ancestry-passenger-list-roma-1903]

A Westchester naturalization index lists a Vincenzo Vigliotti declaration in 1928 and a petition in 1930, after Alphonse Sr. was born in March 1921. The petition index gives a birth on 2 September 1892 at Bunito, probably Bonito in Avellino, which does not match this Vincent's other ages. A second Vincenzo Vigliotti in Westchester married Nunziata Santonastoso in 1923 and may be the petitioner. The 1928 and 1930 papers are therefore treated as an open question, not as a fact about this man. If this Vincent never naturalized, or naturalized only after 1921, that would matter for any later Italian citizenship claim. This site does not claim that anyone is eligible.[^westchester-naturalization-vigliotti]

Vincent J. Vigliotti of 44 Brambach Road died at Grasslands Hospital, Mount Pleasant, on 24 April 1944, after a long illness. The New York State death index records the death under the spelling VIGHIOTTO, certificate 26490. He was survived by Vincenza Guida Vigliotti, four sons then in the armed forces, and five daughters. Funeral services were held at Immaculate Heart of Mary on 28 April 1944.[^nys-death-index-1944-vigliotti][^scarsdale-inquirer-1944-04-28]

The death notice (age 53 in April 1944) points to about 1891. A member tree gives 4 July 1885 at Santa Maria a Vico. A naturalization index for a different or unproven Vincenzo Vigliotti gives 2 September 1892 at Bunito.

people.summary: A carpenter, born in Italy about 1899, he lived in Eastchester, married Susan M. Rescigno in 1926, and died at White Plains Hospital on 29 October 1957, aged 58. Father of Concetta Mignone.
people.story:
Gerard Mignone, a carpenter of Eastchester, was a native of Italy and died at White Plains Hospital on 29 October 1957, aged 58.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1957-11-08] The Westchester marriage index records his marriage to Susan M. Rescigno in 1926, certificate 51289.[^westchester-marriage-51289] He was a parishioner of Immaculate Conception Church in Tuckahoe. He was survived by his wife, Susan Rescigno Mignone, two daughters including Mrs. Alphonse J. Vigliotti (Concetta), six sons, and other family in Italy.

The 1950 census records Gerard, aged 50, born in Italy, with Susan, aged 40, born in New York, and their younger children on Brook Street in Eastchester. Concetta, already married, is not in that household.[^census-1950-mignone] The Westchester naturalization index lists a Gerardo Mignone declaration in 1923 and a petition in 1929.[^westchester-naturalization-mignone]

birth.note: The 1957 notice gives age 58, and the 1950 census gives age 50, both pointing to about 1899. The Italian town is not yet known.

people.story:
Patricia Morrisey Walsh was born in Bronxville, New York, the daughter of James T. and Fernanda (Ehrenfels) Morrisey.[^obituary-patricia-paul-walsh-2019] The Rye Record obituary published on 14 October 2019 says she was 91 when she died on 4 September 2019, which points to a birth year of about 1928.

She graduated from The Ursuline School in New Rochelle in 1946 and earned a bachelor's degree in Business from the College of New Rochelle in 1950. On 5 May 1951 she married Paul H. Walsh. They raised their four children in Larchmont and, about twenty-nine years before 2019, moved to Rye.

A Mass of Christian Burial was celebrated at the Church of the Resurrection on 9 September 2019. She was survived by her four children, including Barbara Walsh Vigliotti and her husband Al, and by five grandchildren, one of them named Dylan.

people.story:
Paul Hingston Walsh was born on 7 January 1927 in Yonkers, New York, the son of Clara (Hingston) and William A. Walsh.[^find-a-grave-paul-walsh-2019][^obituary-patricia-paul-walsh-2019] He graduated from Iona Prep in 1943, then went to Villanova College through the Navy V12 program, earning a Bachelor of Science in 1947 and a degree in Mechanical Engineering a year later. In 1970 he formed his own independent sales representative company, after earlier executive sales work for electronics firms.

He married Patricia Morrisey on 5 May 1951 at Immaculate Heart of Mary Church, Scarsdale.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1951-05-18] They raised their four children in Larchmont and later lived in Rye. He died a little more than three weeks after his wife, on 27 September 2019, and was buried at Greenwood Union Cemetery in Rye after a Mass at the Church of the Resurrection.

people.summary: Born 14 March 1921 in Eastchester, New York, son of Vincent and Vincenza Vigliotti. A World War II veteran of the United States Army. He married Concetta Mignone on 24 August 1947 and died on 1 January 2011 in Dobbs Ferry. He is buried at Gate of Heaven Cemetery, Hawthorne.
people.story:
Alphonse John Vigliotti Sr. was born on 14 March 1921 in Eastchester, New York, the son of Vincent Vigliotti and Vincenza Guida (also spelled Guido).[^obituary-alphonse-vigliotti-sr-2011] His World War II draft card, filed at Tuckahoe on 15 February 1942, gives the same date and names the birthplace as Scarsdale, with Vincent Vigliotti as the person who would always know his address.[^ancestry-wwii-draft-alphonse-vigliotti-1942] Eastchester and Scarsdale sit on the same local line, and the Scarsdale post office served parts of the Town of Eastchester, so these are treated as the same community.

He appears as a child in the Vigliotti household at 44 Brambach Avenue in the 1930 and 1940 censuses.[^ancestry-census-1930-vigliotti][^ancestry-census-1940-vigliotti] In December 1942 the Scarsdale Inquirer reported that he and his brother Andrew had just left for the Army, while Vincent and Tony were already in the Navy.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1942-12-04] His 2011 obituary says he served in the United States Army in Normandy, the Ardennes, Northern France, Central Europe and the Rhineland.

On 24 August 1947 he married Concetta Mignone at Immaculate Heart of Mary Church, Scarsdale. The wedding notice calls him an Army veteran then employed by the Tommasi Motor Company, and a graduate of Eastchester High School.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1947-08-29] He later worked as a manager for A&P in Eastchester, and was a member of the Eastchester Volunteer Fire Department.

He died on 1 January 2011 at Dobbs Ferry Hospital, aged 89. The New York State death index is certificate 037088. A Funeral Mass was celebrated at Immaculate Heart of Mary, and he was buried at Gate of Heaven Cemetery, Hawthorne.[^nys-death-index-2011-alphonse-sr][^obituary-alphonse-vigliotti-sr-2011] The obituary names his children as Alphonse J. Vigliotti Jr., Susan Fucale and Renee Makras, which confirms the sibling link first suggested by Pat Fucale's obituary.

birth.note: The 2011 obituary gives Eastchester. The 15 February 1942 draft card gives Scarsdale. These are treated as the same community, not as a conflict.

people.summary: Daughter of Gerard Mignone and Susan Rescigno. She married Alphonse J. Vigliotti on 24 August 1947 at Immaculate Heart of Mary, Scarsdale. A Find a Grave entry gives her death as 16 November 2012 and burial at Gate of Heaven Cemetery, Hawthorne; that date is still probable.
people.story:
Concetta Mignone, daughter of Gerard and Susan (Rescigno) Mignone, married Alphonse Vigliotti on 24 August 1947 at Immaculate Heart of Mary Church, Scarsdale.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1947-08-29] Both were graduates of Eastchester High School. She is named as Mrs. Alphonse J. Vigliotti in her father's 1957 obituary, and later Mignone obituaries name Concetta Mignone Vigliotti as a predeceased sister.[^scarsdale-inquirer-1957-11-08][^westchester-fh-lawrence-mignone]

She survived her husband, who died on 1 January 2011.[^obituary-alphonse-vigliotti-sr-2011] A Find a Grave memorial places her at Gate of Heaven Cemetery, Hawthorne, Section 28, A, Row I, Grave 29, with a date of 16 November 2012, age 85, and a note that the date may be the interment date. That death is treated as probable until an obituary or civil record is read.[^find-a-grave-concetta-2012]

birth.note: Find a Grave gives age 85 at a 16 November 2012 date, which points to about 1927. No birth record is in hand.

On 30 October 1977 he married Susan Vigliotti of Eastchester. He died in Valhalla, New York, on 21 November 2026, and was buried at Gate of Heaven Cemetery in Hawthorne.
people.story:
Pasquale "Pat" Fucale was born on 22 September 1952 in Cattolica Eraclea, Agrigento, Sicily, to Anthony and Rosa Fucale.[^obituary-pasquale-fucale-2026] At the age of four he and his family immigrated to Montreal, Canada. Six years later they moved again and settled in White Plains, New York, where Pat graduated from White Plains High School in 1970. He later earned a bachelor's degree in Business Administration from Pace University.

He worked in sales for Checkpoint, Symbol Technologies, and, for more than twenty years, Konica Minolta. After he retired he worked as a crossing guard for the Pleasantville School District at the Bedford Road School crossing, and he volunteered as a Sunday morning usher at Holy Name of Jesus Church in Valhalla.

On 30 October 1977 he married Susan Vigliotti, of Eastchester, New York. They had three daughters. Pat died on 21 November 2026 in Valhalla, after a brief battle with pancreatic cancer, at the age of 74. A funeral mass was held at Holy Name of Jesus Church on 24 November 2026, and he was buried the same day at Gate of Heaven Cemetery in Hawthorne, New York.

The obituary lists his brothers-in-law and sisters-in-law as Alphonse Vigliotti (Barbara) and Renee Makras (George). That is the first record on this site that ties the Fucale and Vigliotti families together. The sibling link between Susan, Alphonse and Renee is treated as probable until a birth or other vital record confirms it.
